sections.overview: Apistogramma pulchra is a small South American dwarf cichlid described by Sven Kullander in 1980. It is recorded from the Madeira River basin in Brazil, within the broader Amazon system.
sections.identification: FishBase lists a maximum standard length of 3.2 cm for male or unsexed fish; no reliable female maximum, mass, width or body-height measurement was found. The name pulchra means handsome and alludes to its blended color pattern and slender form.
sections.habitat: The confirmed range is the Madeira River basin, with the type locality on the Rio Preto, a tributary of the Candeias near Porto Velho. Specialist accounts associate the pulchra complex with mostly blackwater habitats, though conditions vary among tributaries.
sections.diet: No direct diet study for this species was located. Small Apistogramma generally pick tiny invertebrates from the bottom, but that genus-level expectation should not be mistaken for measured evidence on A. pulchra.
sections.behavior: FishBase reports cave spawning and female care of eggs and larvae in its species summary, but wild group behavior is little documented.
sections.reproduction: The eggs are laid on the ceiling of a cave and tended by the female. The consulted species summary gives no reliable clutch-size range for Apistogramma pulchra.
sections.ecology: Specialist classifications place pulchra in the informal pulchra complex within the broader agassizii group. It is therefore a useful comparison with A. agassizii, but color forms and uncertain lookalikes should not be assigned by appearance alone.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern, assessed on 29 October 2020. That summary is the latest assessment date available in the cited species account.
